title: Civil Comments JEVPA replication with expanded discovery
description: Given the checksum-pinned Civil Comments validation parquet and the first study split, when a second deterministic 30,000-row sample is frozen disjoint from the first sample before any analyst or Jev call, then it provides 500 discovery labels, 500 slice-enriched selection rows, and 1,000 random final-test rows. The analyst sees only discovery text and binary toxicity label. Four shared initial proposals must add exactly one element each; each arm gets two precommitted branch proposals. Retain nondominated candidates across overall, threat, and identity-attack selection Brier only when both sealed slices have enough toxic support. Record all calls and actual usage; enforce a 4,500 Jev-request ceiling and $35 provider ceiling.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Agent root (Codex, gpt-6-astra): Started the independent replication. The fixed design uses a 500-label discovery set, 500 selection rows, and 1,000 final-test rows drawn from a new 30,000-row sample disjoint from the first study sample. Source annotations remain sealed from the analyst.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Agent root (Codex, gpt-6-astra): Replication complete. Initial candidates showed a distinct threat versus identity-attack Pareto split, but the two-specialist merge lost selection to greedy (Brier 0.18839 vs 0.18308; accuracy 0.728 vs 0.742). Per preregistration, no held-out requests were made. Result document records a three-call analyst duplication deviation and incomplete shared-batch token accounting after an interrupted local window.

comments.text: Reported the preregistered replication result; selection gate failed, so final test remained sealed.
